stories.title: Real yields account for much of current 10Y level while modelled term premium softened
stories.whatChanged: Official TIPS real‑yield observation remains elevated while ACM term‑premium estimates declined recently.
stories.whyItMatters: If real yields — not term premium — explain 10Y, higher real rates imply tighter real borrowing costs and stronger growth/inflation linkage to policy.
stories.mechanism: Higher real‑rate component (inflation expectations and/or real real‑rate drivers) is supporting nominal yields even as modelled term premium falls.
stories.conclusion: Current canonical TIPS real‑yield evidence supports a decomposition where real yields explain much of nominal 10Y; term‑premium evidence exists but intraday/MOVE is needed to determine persistence.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Canonical intraday MOVE and 5m–30m 2Y/10Y bars showing immediate and persistent front‑end-driven repricing would increase confidence; a reversal in real yields would weaken this story.

stories.title: High‑yield spreads widened sharply while IG moves are muted — concentrated credit stress so far
stories.whatChanged: 20‑session HY OAS rose ~63bp while IG OAS moved modestly (~10bp), signalling selective stress in lower‑quality credit.
stories.whyItMatters: Selective HY widening can impair funding for specific issuers or sectors without being a broad systemic credit event; it constrains risk appetite for levered strategies and small/issuer‑specific names.
stories.mechanism: Issuer/sector‑level stress and repricing in HY has driven OAS widening; broader IG market and equity breadth do not yet confirm systemic credit spill‑over.
stories.conclusion: Evidence shows pronounced HY widening across the 20‑session window with IG largely contained; this is consistent with concentrated credit pressure rather than broad credit market failure.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Sustained coordinated IG widening and a canonical MOVE uplift would indicate broadening credit stress.

stories.title: US distillate stocks drew down and geopolitical risk keeps upside to fuel‑related inflation on watch
stories.whatChanged: EIA weekly data show a 2.527m barrel decline in US distillate inventories for the reported week and news analysis highlights multi‑directional squeeze risks from conflicts.
stories.whyItMatters: Product draws plus geopolitical risk can sustain energy inflation exposure and support longer‑run breakevens or real yields if sustained.
stories.mechanism: Lower product stocks tighten physical product balance which, combined with supply risks, can push product prices and feed into CPI measures that influence yields.
stories.conclusion: Observed distillate draws and geopolitical reporting raise the odds of renewed product‑led inflation pressure, but price‑curve/crack confirmation is required.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Canonical crack curve/backwardation evidence or refinery utilisation data showing persistent product tightness would strengthen this story.
